name: Gramercy Cellars Syrah Lagniappe 2015
text:
## Gramercy Cellars Syrah Lagniappe 2015

**The story.** Gramercy Cellars was founded in 2005 in [Walla Walla](https://www.google.com/maps?q=Gramercy+Cellars,+Walla+Walla,+Washington,+USA&t=k), Washington, by Greg Harrington, a [Master Sommelier](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Court_of_Master_Sommeliers), and his wife Pam, an investment banker. Greg had run the wine programmes for celebrated chefs including [Emeril Lagasse](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Emeril_Lagasse) and [Wolfgang Puck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolfgang_Puck); living in Brooklyn in 2004, the couple became intrigued by Walla Walla wines, and a year later they owned a winery there, making Rhône- and Bordeaux-style wines, about 8,000 cases a year from Walla Walla and [Columbia Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Columbia_Valley_AVA) fruit. The Wine Advocate wrote that Harrington "is fashioning some of the top wines in Washington" ([WineBid](https://www.winebid.com/BuyWine/Item/Auction/1238664/2015)).

**The wine: Lagniappe.** "[Lagniappe](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lagniappe)" is a Louisiana word for "a little something extra". Gramercy's Lagniappe is a [Syrah](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Syrah) from the Columbia Valley, an appellation so large (11 million acres, almost half of Washington State) that it contains famous sub-regions like the [Yakima Valley](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Yakima_Valley_AVA) and Walla Walla ([WineBid](https://www.winebid.com/BuyWine/Item/Auction/1238664/2015)).

**The vintage.** Jancis Robinson's vintage charts don't cover Washington. The critics' notes below describe a ripe yet fresh, savoury 2015.

**What the critics say for 2015.** As listed by [WineBid](https://www.winebid.com/BuyWine/Item/Auction/1238664/2015), which quotes excerpts of each note:
- **[Jeb Dunnuck](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Jeb_Dunnuck): 98**. Black raspberries, crushed flowers and [tapenade](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tapenade); "medium to full-bodied, seamless, and silky on the palate, with incredible finesse and elegance".
- **[Wine Advocate](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Wine_Advocate): 95**. "A rich, extravagant bouquet" of ripe plums, blackberries, bay leaf, black olive and cola; full-bodied and layered, with succulent fruit concealing fine-grained, chewy tannins.
- **[Vinous](https://vinous.com): 93**. Blueberry, blackberry, mint and minerals; dry but rich, with serious tannins and a long, rising finish.
- **[Wine Enthusiast](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wine_Enthusiast): 90**. Fresh herbs, blood orange, olives, cured meat, hay and black pepper; dark raspberry and cherry with dry, bunched-up tannins.
- **[CellarTracker](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/CellarTracker) community: 92.5** (from your CellarTracker list).

**How it's drinking now.** In October 2026 the wine is eleven years old. Your CellarTracker list gives a window of 2021 to 2031. So it is in its prime: black fruit, olive, bay, pepper and cured meat, the tannins now softened. Decant about an hour ahead and serve at 16 to 17°C.

**Food.** Savoury Syrah loves grilled lamb, smoked brisket, duck with olives, or a pepper-crusted steak.

**Value and where to buy.** Lagniappe isn't listed in the stores on this site, but BSW Liquor carries Gramercy's Lower East Syrah 2020 at $33.

**Curious details**
- **From sommelier to winemaker.** Harrington went from running restaurant wine lists for star chefs to making some of Washington's top wines ([WineBid](https://www.winebid.com/BuyWine/Item/Auction/1238664/2015)).
- **A Washington giant.** The Columbia Valley AVA, established in 1984, covers 18,000 square miles, larger than some US states ([WineBid](https://www.winebid.com/BuyWine/Item/Auction/1238664/2015)).

Sources:
- [WineBid, 2015 Gramercy Lagniappe (critics' excerpts and history)](https://www.winebid.com/BuyWine/Item/Auction/1238664/2015)
